description: Issue #839: at RUN TIME a profile keyword is a built-in name unconditionally. `execute()` has no active profile set — it runs every profile's primitives and the reader recognises all six block heads regardless of profile — so the declaration-slot guard cannot be gated on one, and `spec/grammar.md`'s rule (maintainer ruling #833 rule 4) says it must not be: "a name that could be declared in one implementation but not in another would be invisible and unpredictable to a learner". So `define ask` halts at phase-1 registration with `ol-reserved-word` and the `ask` call on line 4 never runs. This fixture was added because a mutation removing profile keywords from the runtime's built-in-name lookup passed the ENTIRE conformance corpus: `sprites/reserved-procedures-with-sprites` and its `-without-sprites` pair are both `"check": true`, so nothing in the corpus executed one of these names. KNOWN RESIDUAL, deliberately documented rather than hidden, and MEASURED rather than described: under `profiles: ["core-language"]` alone, `check()` accepts all 22 of `ask each tell when every on_key on_click who beep grid dict wait new_turtle turtles note play rest set_tempo measure axes pr bf` while `execute()` rejects every one -- so the residual is not confined to the three Sprites keywords, and `checker-reserved-word.ts`'s remaining hand-composed gate is uneven across profiles rather than simply "on for profile words" (`define forward`, `define hint`, `define challenge` and `define fd` ARE rejected by both stages under Core alone). The two stages therefore disagree for those 22 names in the direction OPPOSITE to the one #839 closed. Retiring that gate is issue #841's always-on built-in-names list; when it lands, `reserved-procedures-without-sprites` inverts and this fixture is unaffected.

diagnostics.message: ask is already part of OpenLogo. choose another name.
